parsed.why: Strong state protections (shield law, gender-identity hate crimes, no state bathroom ban) lift it above the national line. National passport, entry, custody and facility rules still bind every visitor, so it stays in Elevated Risk.

No statewide adult facility ban, no adult care ban and marriage access are mildly positive. Missing gender-identity coverage in most localities, a hate-crime gap, a draft youth-care regulation and national rules keep it near the band line.

Enacted 2025 bathroom restriction covering state-owned buildings and colleges is a universal exposure. Birth-certificate marker change is closed by court ruling, the hate-crime law omits gender identity and a state body was found to discriminate, placing it below the national line.

Among the most protective states: shield law covering out-of-state care, gender-identity hate crimes, all-gender facilities, self-attestation and an early sodomy repeal. Visitors still face national passport, entry and custody exposure, so it sits in the Elevated band.

Statewide facility ban, a state EO covering prisons and shelters, birth-certificate closure, adult care ban in state facilities, sports exclusion and no gender-identity discrimination or hate-crime coverage. Stacked on national rules, it sits at the High Risk floor.
